transcript.text: d/w not cleaning pls help, gritty bits left on glasses n bowls, beko

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. This issue is usually caused by a blocked filter or clogged spray arm jets. You should check the bottom of the tub for debris and ensure the filters are clean before running another cycle. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drain filter (clean first - gritty/sandy residue). Take out the lower rack, twist and lift out the filter in the bottom of the tub, and rinse it under a tap — a clogged filter starves the spray arms of water. Was the filter dirty or clogged (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
ok just looked, filter was full of food n grease. will clean it now

Turn each spray arm by hand — it should spin freely — and look at the little jet holes. Most arms unclip so you can rinse them and clear the holes with a cocktail stick. Was an arm stuck or were the jets blocked (and are they clear now), is an arm cracked or broken, or were they all fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Check and rinse the spray arm" — The spray arm spins to fire water through small jet holes. Check it spins freely and rinse the jets clear of food/grit. It usually unclips at the centre. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
lower arm spins fine but the upper one is stiff. several holes on it were blocked with seeds/limescale, cleared them with a cocktail stick
Can you tell me whether food redeposited on the dishes?
not sure what u mean, i haven't run it again yet since cleaning the filter n arm. do u want me to run a wash?

Yes, you should run a wash cycle now. This will allow you to verify if the cleaning issue is resolved after clearing the blockages in the upper spray arm and filter. Can you tell me whether by far the most common poor-wash cause (~60%)?
ok, ill run a wash now. not sure what ur last bit means tho, can u say that again?

I did not ask that question in this conversation. The most common causes for gritty residue are blocked spray arm holes, a dirty filter, or using the wrong detergent. Check the detergent flap opens freely when you press its catch, and that nothing tall in the front of the racks blocks it from opening during the wash. Was something blocking it or was it sticking (and is it sorted), is the flap or catch broken, or does it open fine?
not sure about the flap tbh, didnt check it. is it worth running the wash first to see if its better now?

Yes, it is worth running a wash cycle to test the improvement after clearing the blockages. However, since you have not checked the detergent flap, ensure that area is also clear before starting the machine. Quick, eco and glass programmes are gentler — they often won't shift dried-on food on a full load. Have you been using a quick or eco programme (and will you try a normal or intensive one), or already using a normal / intensive programme?
been using the quick 30 min wash tbh. ill run a normal one now n see if its better
Now run a normal programme with a typical load. Are the dishes coming out clean now, or still dirty?
ran a normal wash after cleaning the filter n arm and its much better, loads cleaner now
Good news, that has sorted it. If it happens again, start with the same check. Is there anything else I can help with?
